answer: The juniper counter is kept in spiral and summit reveals each reset. Someone therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 24 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 24 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A farm of 724 identities would post 3367 proofs and burn roughly 84 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
